answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to post a refundable stake and earn reputation through verified completed work before handling valuable tasks. Creating one identity is cheap, but creating thousands means locking capital for every copy, and misbehaviour forfeits the stake and burns that history. Like jade laid over shale, trust builds slowly and cannot be faked quickly, so an attacker flooding the network reaches a nadir of returns, spending more on deposits than any fraud can recover.
